issues.label: Two-step due process suppression framework
issues.why: Court must confirm the correct Kaneaiakala test: first suggestiveness, then reliability under totality of circumstances.

issues.label: Whether show-up was impermissibly suggestive
issues.why: Handcuffed lone suspect, officer behind, in custody, and no warning implicate the threshold suggestiveness inquiry.

issues.label: Failure to give may-or-may-not-be-present warning
issues.why: Officer admitted he could not instruct CW the perpetrator might not be present, a key suggestiveness factor.

issues.label: Language barrier's effect on identification
issues.why: CW's Chuukese-only fluency and absence of interpreter during show-up bear on suggestiveness and reliability.

issues.label: Statement that police 'had a male in custody'
issues.why: Telling CW a suspect was detained may have primed her identification.

issues.label: Reliability analysis under HAWJIC 3.19 factors
issues.why: Court must assess opportunity to observe, stress, description accuracy, cross-racial nature, certainty, and time lapse.

issues.label: Applicability of HAWJIC 3.19A show-up factors
issues.why: Central dispute is whether the circuit court had to apply the show-up-specific suggestiveness factors.

issues.label: Whether express findings on 3.19A required
issues.why: State's first question asks if the court must expressly address each 3.19A factor in its ruling.

issues.label: Whether court actually considered suggestiveness
issues.why: State contends the circuit court did weigh suggestiveness despite only citing 3.19.

issues.label: Relationship between suggestiveness and reliability
issues.why: State argues reliability notwithstanding suggestiveness was the real issue, not suggestiveness alone.

issues.label: Burden of proof on admissibility
issues.why: Court must identify which party bears the burden regarding suggestiveness and reliability at suppression.

issues.label: Standard of review of suppression ruling
issues.why: Mixed questions of law and fact govern appellate review of the identification admissibility decision.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: State's fourth question asks whether any error was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt given other evidence.

issues.label: Strength of independent identification evidence
issues.why: Neighbors lost sight of assailant, lacked clear view; bears on both reliability and harmlessness.

issues.label: Cross-racial/ethnic identification concerns
issues.why: HAWJIC 3.19 flags cross-racial identification as affecting accuracy, potentially relevant here.

issues.label: CW's brief and interpreted description
issues.why: Reliability turns on how well the assailant description matched Jercy given interpretation issues.

issues.label: Proper remedy on remand
issues.why: ICA vacated without specifying admissibility; court must clarify whether suppression or reconsideration is required.

issues.label: Consistency with prior appellate decisions
issues.why: All four certiorari questions frame ICA as inconsistent with precedent, requiring reconciliation.

issues.label: Time and distance between crime and show-up
issues.why: One-to-two-minute proximity and short chase gap affect reliability and possible misidentification.

issues.label: Whether misidentification risk warrants exclusion
issues.why: Ultimate question is if suggestiveness created substantial likelihood of irreparable misidentification.
